title: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction
summary: Researchers are developing a wind-model proof of concept for the Red Sea coast and Gulf of Suez, with operational validation still planned.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The project proposes AI forecasting of wind speed and direction for wind farms, grids, and extreme-weather planning. A prototype and historical benchmark comparisons are in development. Generation, dispatch, and safety benefits remain unquantified.
purpose: Improve wind forecasts for energy operations and severe-weather planning.
system: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction
location: Red Sea coast, Saudi Arabia, and Gulf of Suez, Egypt (planned study regions)

ratings.reason: The Red Sea/Gulf of Suez wind model is a proof of concept under development, without an observed wind-farm operational gain.
Grid resilience and climate-risk reduction are potential uses.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 21: Driven Meteorological Modeling: Transforming Wind Speed and Direction Prediction

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: Wind-forecast AI targets energy and climate decisions
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
